newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deputy urges British-style arms sales curbs.
newsitem.headline: French deputy urges British-style arms sales curbs.

text.p: The head of the National Assembly's foreign affairs committee urged the French government on Monday to copy Britain's ban on arms sales to states with poor human rights records which might use them against their citizens.

Jack Lang, who was culture minister under the late President Francois Mitterrand, also wrote to the new socialist ministers of foreign affairs and defence urging that France destroy its stock of anti-personnel mines.
He praised the new British Labour government's efforts to limit the arms trade as an excellent idea and hoped they would be copied both by other European countries and around the world.

British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook announced on July 28 London would ban arms sales to countries liable to use them against their own people or in an aggressive way against another country. It would also ban the export of electric shock batons, stun guns, leg irons and other instruments of torture.

"It is important for the French government, which is now inspired by a new ethical view of international relations, to support this position...in conjunction with our British friends and partners in the European Union," Lang wrote to Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine and Defence Minister Alain Richard.
According to the new guidelines, Britain would pay special attention to equipment with potential for use in cracking down on protesters, such as armoured personnel carriers.
Both Britain and France are leading weapons exporters.
